item.title: OFC Men's Champions League: Nabenu calls for greater hunger as Rewa target crucial win
item.description: Rewa suffered a disappointing 4–1 defeat in their opening match against Vanuatu's Galaxy FC, despite creating several scoring opportunities. With their hopes of progressing further into the tournament now under pressure, Nabenu says the team understands the importance of securing all three points.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa suffered a disappointing 4–1 defeat in their opening match against Vanuatu's Galaxy FC, despite creating several scoring opportunities.

With their hopes of progressing further into the tournament now under pressure, Nabenu says the team understands the importance of securing all three points.

Nabenu believes Rewa do not need a major overhaul, but says the team must be more clinical when opportunities come their way.

He also urged supporters to turn out and back Rewa in their crucial encounter.

Rewa FC will take on Tupapa Maraerenga FC at 4pm at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

The Delta Tigers will play their final group match against Lae City FC of Papua New Guinea on Saturday at 3pm at the same venue.

They need positive results in both matches to keep their hopes of reaching the semi-finals alive.

item.title: Ra High ready to roar again - Wakili the man to watch
item.description: Ra High School will head into this week’s National Vodafone Super Deans Competition clash with plenty of confidence after producing one of the biggest statements of last week’s quarter-finals. The Ra boys stunned former Super Deans champions Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), sending a clear message that they are not in the competition just to make up the numbers.
item.content:encoded:
Ra High School will head into this week’s National Vodafone Super Deans Competition clash with plenty of confidence after producing one of the biggest statements of last week’s quarter-finals.

The Ra boys stunned former Super Deans champions Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), sending a clear message that they are not in the competition just to make up the numbers.

One player who caught the eye in that impressive victory was inside centre Jack Wakili, who crossed the try line twice against RKS.

Wakili, who hails from Maniava Takaimalo in Ra, has impressive speed and attacking instincts, along with a sneaky sidestep.

He will form a formidable midfield combination with Joseva Boto from Bua at outside centre, giving Ra High a dangerous one-two punch in the backs.

The pair will be expected to test the Lions’ defensive line with their strength, speed and ability to create opportunities in broken play.

Ra High School will play Suva Grammar School at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

The time for the match has not been confirmed yet.

item.title: Flying Fijian Wainiqolo completes challenging Naboro Obstacle Course
item.description: France-based Flying Fijian and Olympian Jiuta Wainiqolo completes the challenging Naboro Obstacle Course at the Naboro Corrections Facility. The obstacle course at the Fiji Corrections training facility is a demanding test designed to challenge mental toughness, resilience, determination and physical fitness.
item.content:encoded:
France-based Flying Fijian and Olympian Jiuta Wainiqolo completes the challenging Naboro Obstacle Course at the Naboro Corrections Facility.

The obstacle course at the Fiji Corrections training facility is a demanding test designed to challenge mental toughness, resilience, determination and physical fitness.

Wainiqolo is currently in the country and never lets his guard down when it comes to maintaining his fitness and discipline.

During his visit, Wainiqolo also met fellow Olympian Josua Vakurunabili, who currently serves with the Fiji Corrections Service Emergency Control Unit.

Known in France as the “Fijian Ferrari”, Wainiqolo was also part of the Ratu Kadavulevu School team that won the Super Deans title in 2015.

item.title: All Blacks thump Sharks 54-0 in Durban
item.description: New Zealand ran in eight tries as they swept aside South Africa’s Sharks to win 54-0 in their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour clash in wet Durban this morning. The match was played in tough conditions that made running rugby difficult and led to numerous errors, but it was still a commanding display from the tourists, who never looked troubled in the contest.
item.content:encoded:
New Zealand ran in eight tries as they swept aside South Africa’s Sharks to win 54-0 in their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour clash in wet Durban this morning.

The match was played in tough conditions that made running rugby difficult and led to numerous errors, but it was still a commanding display from the tourists, who never looked troubled in the contest.

It followed a less impressive 38-21 win over the Stormers in Cape Town on Friday, a scoreline that flattered the All Blacks, with the scores level at 14-14 after 65 minutes.

There was a poignant moment before the game in Durban when All Blacks legend Ma’a Nonu, who played 103 tests for the side before retiring from international rugby in 2015, led a one-man haka in response to the New Zealand side’s challenge.

Clearly emotional, the 44-year-old wiped away tears after completing the haka.

He came onto the field after 61 minutes, having joined the Sharks on a short-term contract in a player/mentor role last month.

Wing Fehi Fineanganofo scored the first of his two tries in the 18th minute before Damian McKenzie added a second to give the All Blacks a 14-0 halftime lead.

They made a fast start to the second half when Caleb Clarke crossed for a third try, before Fineanganofo added his second following a period of scrappy play as the slippery ball eluded both teams.

The under-strength Sharks were being stretched at this point, and Beauden Barrett crossed to score a fifth try within the first hour.

There were more tries for scrum-half Kyle Preston, Timoci Tavatavanawai and Sam Darry as the home side barely got out of their half in the second period.

item.title: No indication yet on Messi’s return to Inter Miami
item.description: There is no indication yet on when Lionel Messi will return to Inter Miami following the death of his father, Jorge Messi. Inter Miami defender Facundo Mura says the entire team has been deeply affected by the news and is supporting Messi during the difficult period.
item.content:encoded:
There is no indication yet on when Lionel Messi will return to Inter Miami following the death of his father, Jorge Messi.

Inter Miami defender Facundo Mura says the entire team has been deeply affected by the news and is supporting Messi during the difficult period.

Jorge Messi died a t a hospital in Rosario, Argentina, at the age of 68.

Mura says the team is standing with Messi from afar and wants its captain to know that he has their full support.

Inter Miami manager Guillermo Hoyos says the news has caused great pain within the club.

Neither Mura nor Hoyos provided any indication on when Messi is expected to return to the team.

item.title: Tavua Town Council says it would never risk lives amid Garvey Park safety concerns
item.description: The Tavua Town Council says they would never imperil the health of anyone's life or limb if they had knowledge of the dangers posed from the use of any of its assets, in this case Garvey Park. This is after concerns were raised in regards to the safety of students playing over the weekend at Garvey Park in Tavua which was the venue of some of the Vodafone Super Deans quarterfinals as well as the W
item.content:encoded:
The Tavua Town Council says they would never imperil the health of anyone's life or limb if they had knowledge of the dangers posed from the use of any of its assets, in this case Garvey Park.

This is after concerns were raised in regards to the safety of students playing over the weekend at Garvey Park in Tavua which was the venue of some of the Vodafone Super Deans quarterfinals as well as the Weetbix Raluve competition, where students were seen digging out large stones from the ground.

While responding to fijivillage News, Acting Council CEO, Sireli Korovulavula says they are also deeply concerned about the discovery of the stone in the centre of the playing field before the start of the games on Saturday.

Korovulavula says the ground has within the last few weeks hosted Kaji Rugby for the Tavua/Vatukoula District an d the Western Secondary School League games and there was no indication of the presence of the stone during the two sporting events.

He says in hindsight, they are in total agreement that more vigilance ought to have been taken by the Council and that is what it will do going forward.

Assistant Minister for Youth and Sports, Aliki Bia had raised the alarm early Saturday morning after students were seen digging out large stones f rom the ground saying this is not good and it does not portray a good image for the development of our rugby.

Bia says the welfare of students and players is paramount.

item.title: Emerging rugby talent to take centre stage alongside Fijiana XV
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/08/2026 The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Interim Committee has clarified that, as part of the Vodafone Super Deans semi-final programme, selected matches will be played alongside the second Test between the Vodafone Fijiana XV and South Africa’s Springbok Women this Saturday at Churchill Park in Lautoka.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/08/2026

The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Interim Committee has clarified that, as part of the Vodafone Super Deans semi-final programme, selected matches will be played alongside the second Test between the Vodafone Fijiana XV and South Africa’s Springbok Women this Saturday at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

This gives Fiji’s emerging rugby talent a unique opportunity to perform on one of the country’s biggest rugby stages.

Interim Committee representative Biu Colati says the programme has been designed with the long-term development of school rugby at its heart.

He says their priority has always been to provide the best possible experience for student-athletes while continuing to strengthen the development pathway for school rugby.

Colati says the programme gives young players the rare opportun ity to perform on the same stage as the national team, exposing them to the atmosphere and standards of international rugby while celebrating the very best of school rugby.

He adds that the experience will inspire many of these players as they continue their rugby journey.

Colati says they sincerely thank the Ministry of Education, the Fiji Rugby Football Union, participating schools, competition officials, sponsors, volunteers and supporters for working together to make the programme possible.

Looking at the semi-finals at Churchill Park in Lautoka, Ratu Navula College will face Ratu Kadavulevu School in the Under-14 grade, Ratu Navula College will meet Lelean Memorial School in the Under-19 division, Sigatoka Methodist College will play St Vincent College in the Weet-Bix Raluve Under-16 and Suva Grammar School will take on Ra High School in the Under-18 grade.

At 1pm on Saturday, the Vodafone Fijiana XV will take on the Springbok Women in the second Test of the series.

The remaining Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve semi-final fixtures will be played at HFC Bank Stadium, Buckhurst Ground 1 and Bidesi Ground in Suva.

In the Super Deans semi-finals in Suva, Queen Victoria School will face MGM High School in the Under-14 grade.

In the Under-15 grade, Lelean Memorial School will meet Marist Brothers High School, while QVS will face Ratu Kadavulevu School.

In the Under-16 grade, Nasinu Secondary School will take on Suva Grammar School, while QVS will meet MGM High School.

In the Under-17 grade, Ba Methodist High School will play RKS, while QVS will face Suva Grammar School.

RKS will meet Navatu Secondary School in the Under-19 grade, while Lelean Memorial School will face Nasinu Secondary School in the Under-18 grade.

In the Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals, Adi Cakobau School will face Nasinu Secondary School in the Under-16 grade.

In the Under-18 grade, MGM High School will meet ACS, while Sila Central High School will take on Lomary Secondary School.
